text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said the ministry will prepare the final draft of the 1997 state budget by the end of this week. The law is expected to be presented to parliament by November 15.

- Marian Sasik, Secretary General of the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE), said the amendment to securities law, passed by parliament on Wednesday, is a significant step back in the pace of development of the Slovak stock market, mainly in the field of protection of minority shareholders and market transparency.
- Sasik also said the new legislation will prevent companies from raising finance on the capital market.
- President Michal Kovac will pay a two-day official visit to the Netherlands, starting on November 12.

- A district court in the central Slovak town Banska Bystrica has ruled that the independent daily Sme has to pay altogether 7.5 million crowns to 18 government members for violating their individual rights.
- Russian airline Aeroflot has canceled its regular route from Bratislava to Chicago, via Shannon in Ireland, and back due to lack of passangers.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) said its restructuring procedures, started last year, have so far brough positive results in reducing growth in the money supply and restructuring banks' loan portfolios.
- The state fund of market regulation said it had already bought 250,000 tonnes of grain from this year's harvest out of a planned 400,000 tonnes.
- The Slovak chemical and pharmaceutical industry is expected to increase its exports by 10 to 12 percent by the year 2000.
